title: Of the Bitter Fruits of Impatience

keywords: of the ill effects of impatience
full_text:
On the fourth day, the Fourth Wazir addressed King Azadbakht on the dangers of hasty execution. Bakhtiyar stood before the throne and deepened the counsel:

'Sire, impatience is a fever of the blood that makes a man leap into the well to escape the rain. It is born of childish pride that demands the harvest before the seed has taken root in the soil.

The impatient general attacks before his scouts have returned, and leads his army into a mountain ambush; the impatient merchant sells his cargo before the market opens, and forfeits his profit; the impatient judge strikes with the sword before hearing the witness, and sheds innocent blood.

How many friendships of thirty years have been shattered in thirty seconds by an impatient tongue? And how many kingdoms have been overthrown because a monarch could not wait until tomorrow to verify a rumor?

He who masters his temper masters his kingdom; but he who is mastered by impatience is a slave to every passing breeze, as the history of Prince Bihzad illustrates with tragic clarity.'
moral: Hasty impatience blinds reason, breaks alliances, and plunges the rash into sudden destruction.
